Founded in 1872, the school was named after Imre Madách, a renowned Hungarian poet and playwright, whose works had a profound impact on the country's literary heritage. It was here, amidst the academic rigor and cultural richness of Madách Imre High School, that Szakonyi's passion for writing began to take root. During his time at the school, Szakonyi was exposed to a wide range of literary influences, from the works of Hungarian masters like Sándor Márai and Dezső Kosztolányi to the classical plays of Shakespeare and Molière. The school's emphasis on language, literature, and drama helped Szakonyi develop his writing skills, and he soon began to experiment with his own creative voice. One of Szakonyi's earliest literary endeavors was a school newspaper, which he co-founded with his classmates. This humble publication became a platform for the young writer to express himself, sharing his thoughts on literature, politics, and social issues. The experience not only honed his writing skills but also instilled in him a sense of responsibility and discipline, essential qualities for a writer. Szakonyi's time at Madách Imre High School was also marked by his involvement in the school's drama club. Under the guidance of dedicated teachers, he participated in numerous productions, both on and off stage. He smiled, his mind still half-lost in the world of his story. "Yes, thank you, my love. And perhaps some of those lovely Japanese biscuits you brought back from the market?" As he waited for Erzsébet to bring in the tray, Károly's gaze fell upon the small, framed photograph on his desk. It was a faded snapshot of himself and Emiko, taken on the deck of a research vessel in Tokyo Bay. They were both grinning from ear to ear, their faces wind-whipped and sun-kissed. He felt a pang of nostalgia, but it was tempered by the knowledge that those experiences had shaped him into the writer he was today. With a sense of renewed purpose, Károly turned back to his manuscript, the words flowing effortlessly as the characters of his story came alive once more.
